cards.text: It's spring, the time when kings march out to war. David sends out Joab, the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16), with the whole army of Israel. They destroy the Ammonites and lay siege to the city of Rabbah.

cards.question: The whole army of Israel is out at Rabbah. So where's King David?

cards.text: One evening David gets up from his bed and strolls around on the palace roof, where he sees a woman bathing, a very beautiful woman. He sends someone to ask about her, and he's told her name: Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam.

cards.question: Besides her name, David is told one more thing about Bathsheba, the woman he saw from the roof. What is it?

answers.text: She's the wife of Uriah the Hittite
She's a servant in the palace

cards.text: Then David sends messengers to get her, and when she comes to him, he sleeps with her. She had just purified herself from her uncleanness, and then she returns home.

cards.question: Then Bathsheba sends word to David, saying, "I am ___."

cards.text: David sends orders to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." When Uriah arrives, David asks how Joab and the troops are doing and how the war is going.

cards.question: Then David has a word for Uriah. He tells him, "Go down to your ___ and wash your feet."

cards.text: So Uriah leaves the palace, and a gift from the king follows him out.

cards.question: Uriah has left the palace. Where does he sleep?

answers.text: At the palace door with the servants
At home in his own house
In a tent outside the city

cards.text: Then David is told, "Uriah did not go home." I bet the king is nervous now, and he asks Uriah, "Haven't you just arrived from a journey?" and then, "Why didn't you go home?"

cards.question: Uriah tells David the ark, Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and Joab's soldiers are camped in the open field. So what does Uriah say he can't do?

answers.text: Go home to his house and his wife
Go back out to the battle
Take a gift from the king

cards.text: Then Uriah swears, "As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!"

cards.question: True or false: after Uriah refuses to go home, David tells him to stay in Jerusalem one more day.

cards.text: So Uriah stays in Jerusalem that day and the next, and David invites him to eat and drink with him. Then David gets Uriah drunk.

cards.question: True or false: that evening, drunk, Uriah finally goes home to his house.

cards.text: The next morning, David writes a letter to Joab and sends it with Uriah. The letter goes to Joab in Uriah's own hands.

cards.question: What does David's letter tell Joab to do with Uriah?

answers.text: Put him at the front of the fiercest battle
Send him home to his wife for a while
Make him a commander over the army

cards.question: True or false: David's letter tells Joab to keep the other soldiers close beside Uriah.

cards.text: As Joab besieges the city, he puts Uriah where he knows the strongest enemy soldiers are.

cards.question: The men of the city come out and fight against Joab. What happens to Uriah?

cards.text: Some of David's servants fall in the fighting too. Then Joab sends David a full account of the battle and gives the messenger instructions.

cards.question: Joab tells the messenger that if the king's anger flares, David may ask him something. What might David ask?

answers.text: Why they got so close to the wall
Why they left the ark behind

cards.text: Joab says that if the king's anger flares, David may even bring up Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth, who died at Thebez when a woman dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall.

cards.question: Joab tells the messenger that if King David asks why they got so close to the wall, he should say, "Your servant ___ the Hittite is dead as well."

cards.text: The messenger tells David everything: the enemy came out, Israel drove them back to the gate, then archers shot from the wall and some of the king's servants were killed. Then he adds, "And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well."

cards.question: David hears the news about Uriah. What message does he send back to Joab?

answers.text: Don't let this matter upset you
You were careless with my men
Pull back from the city at once

cards.text: David also says the sword devours one as well as another. And he sends Joab this: "Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it."

cards.question: True or false: when Bathsheba hears that her husband is dead, she mourns for him.

cards.text: When the time of mourning is over, David has her brought to his house, and she becomes his wife and bears him a son.

cards.question: One last line closes the passage: "But the thing that David had done was ___ in the sight of the LORD."

cards.text: And friend, this story isn't over. Not even close.
